title: Lesson 11 Overview
subtitle: Listen to the lesson explained in English

transcript.en: Hey! 👋 Welcome to Lesson 11 — Furniture & the Past Tense.
Three things: **kitchen and bedroom furniture**, the **past tense**, and Malta's **old means of transport**. Let's go!
Keep an eye on the plurals — many are broken. Oven, forn, becomes fran; table, mejda, becomes imwejjed.
This is the big one. The Maltese past tense is built on the **mamma** — the plain 'he' form. It's the answer to 'What did he do yesterday?'
To get the other persons, you add a suffix. **I** adds -t, **she** adds -et, **we** add -na, **they** add -u.
Notice the three consonants k, t, b never move — only the vowels around them shift. That root-and-pattern idea comes from Arabic.
A few verbs are irregular. Mar — 'he went' — has a weak letter in its root, so it changes a lot:
That's 'I went' — quite different from mar!
Before buses, Malta had horse carriages, a tram, even a railway. The horse-drawn carriage:
And the route bus you still take today:
Furniture, the past tense, old transport. Now try the sections. **Prosit!** 🇲🇹
